predecessors.name: Holy Roman Empire
predecessors.text: Liège and the county of Huy

successors.name: French First Republic
successors.text: Liège, Huy, Haspinga, Bouillon, Moha and Loon

ledger.x: 1040: Henry III's charter 'granted this county to the Cathedral of Saint-Lambert'.
By 1190 Loon is under the bishop.
1366: the overlordship ends in incorporation (Loon page).
1366: Loon becomes part of the principality.

ledger.cp: House of La Marck (châtellenie of Bouillon)

ledger.x: 1521: Érard de La Marck, Prince-Bishop of Liège, 'managed to regain Bouillon for the Prince-Bishopric' with Charles V's troops.
ledger.cp: House of La Marck (châtellenie of Bouillon)

ledger.x: 1551: Henry II of France occupies Bouillon.
1568: the County of Horne is acquired (infobox); the page gives no terms and no place.
28 November 1792: Dumouriez, after Jemappes on 6 November, 'entered Liège on 28 November, amidst popular enthusiasm' and Prince-Bishop de Méan fled.
March 1793: the French are beaten at Neerwinden and the Austrians reinstate the prince-bishop.

27 July 1794: after Fleurus on 26 June the Austrians leave Liège, bombarding and burning the Amercoeur district; the battle of Sprimont on 17 September is the last before the principality is conquered.

wars.name: Rudolf of Zähringen's campaign against Loon
wars.outcome: Prince-Bishop Rudolf of Zähringen's campaign 'devastated the county's old capital at Borgloon in 1179'; by 1190 the count was under the bishop's overlordship.

wars.name: War of the Moha succession
wars.outcome: Albert II of Dagsburg died without a son in 1212; Henry I of Brabant and Louis II of Loon both claimed Moha; at Steppes on 13 October 1213 the Liège side (with Loon and Henry III of Limburg) beat the Brabantine army and Moha was annexed to Liège.

wars.name: Annexation of Loon
wars.outcome: Engelbert III seized Loon in 1362; Arnold VI of Rumigny renounced in favour of Liège and Engelbert incorporated it in 1366.

wars.name: La Marck war over Liège and Bouillon
wars.outcome: William de La Marck ordered the assassination of Bishop Louis de Bourbon in 1482 and John of Hornes was elected; the Treaty of Tongeren of 21 May 1484 ended the war, the La Marcks gave up their claim on Liège and kept Bouillon Castle as a pledge for a…

wars.name: Liège Revolution
wars.outcome: The revolution began on 18 August 1789 and the prince-bishop Hoensbroeck left on 26-27 August; Prussians occupied Liège from November 1789 to April 1790; Austrian forces entered on 12 January 1791 (the page also has 12 February) and Hoensbroeck regained power.

wars.name: French Revolutionary Wars in Liège
wars.outcome: The French entered Liège on 28 November 1792, were beaten at Neerwinden in March 1793, won at Fleurus on 26 June 1794, and the Convention decreed Liège's annexation in 1795.

certainty.note: No page gives a border before the final form; every region is a circle round a named place, and the core circle is the researcher's.
